brief.headline: Tech leads a narrow rally; ASML earnings in two days dominate portfolio risk
brief.regime_summary: SPY sits 1.6% above its 50-day MA and 8.2% above its 200-day MA, up 1.2% on the week. VIX at 15.44 is fractionally below its 20-day average of 15.57, signalling no near-term fear premium. Breadth is the telling caveat: only 3 of 11 sectors trade above their 50-day MAs. XLK and XLV are the only sectors with positive 20-day momentum; XLF, XLRE, XLB and XLC are all in the red. This is a narrow, tech-driven tape. Breakouts in that environment can persist but they carry concentration risk. Treat broad-market support as tentative until breadth widens.

portfolio.note: Price at $535.07, RSI 67.5, just 0.4% off its 20-day high. Earnings on 2026-10-28 are the pivot. At 19% above its 100-day MA and trailing P/E of 29.8x near the top of recent history (pe_vs_hist +0.05), the bar for a gap-up reaction is elevated.

Earnings on 2026-10-14, two days out. Price is $1,780, down 4.7% this week and 5.0% off its 20-day high of $1,873. Trailing P/E of 57.8x is 47% above its historical median of 39.3x. All 30-day EPS revisions were downgrades (1 down, 0 up). Manage size before the print; a miss on EUV order intake would pressure a name already showing mixed MA structure.

XLE at $65.08 bounced 3.6% this week on crude strength, but remains 26% below cost basis at $88. Sector 20-day momentum is barely positive (+0.5%) and 20-day RS vs. market is negative at -1.6%. No structural improvement yet.

GLD at $384.58 is 3.6% below its 20-day MA and 4.6% off its 20-day high. Gold futures (GC=F) show the same picture: 20-day momentum at -3.6%, RSI 41.8. The position is profitable (+67%) but momentum is negative on both 20 and 40-day frames. Watch the $370 area (near 100-day MA) as the level that would require a thesis reassessment.

watchlist.name: Palantir Technologies Inc.
watchlist.thesis: PLTR gained 10.8% this week on above-average volume (rel_volume 1.56), breaking out to within 0.25% of its 20-day high at $209.58. 20-day momentum is +25%, RS vs. market +22.9%. Three analyst EPS estimate upgrades in 30 days vs. zero downgrades. Revenue growth estimated at 83.6% this year. Earnings on 2026-11-02 are a catalyst to watch.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA $187.00, 20-day high $209.58, ATR-based stop ~$202 (1 ATR of $6.67 below current)
watchlist.risk: RSI at 76.3 is overbought; any market risk-off rotation would hit a name trading at 36x its 20-day MA.

watchlist.name: CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc.
watchlist.thesis: CRWD scores highest on the screen at 1.78. 20-day momentum +33%, 34% above its 100-day MA, RS vs. market +30.9%. 48 EPS estimate upgrades against 1 downgrade in 30 days. Earnings not until 2026-12-01, leaving a long runway before event risk.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA $257.71, 20-day high $286.99, ATR-based stop ~$263 (1 ATR of $11.55 below current)
watchlist.risk: Volume is only 0.66x average; the move lacks conviction and could stall without a fresh catalyst. Volatility at 60% annualised makes position sizing critical.

watchlist.name: Shopify Inc.
watchlist.thesis: SHOP up 12.9% this week, within 0.1% of its 20-day high at $170.97. 20-day momentum +32.7%, 31% above 100-day MA. P/E vs. history slightly below median (-3.3%), which is unusual for a name at this momentum rank. Earnings 2026-11-03.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA $146.60 (implied from pct_vs_dma20 of +16.5%), 20-day high ~$171, ATR-based stop ~$164 (1 ATR of $6.47 below current)
watchlist.risk: RSI 72.8 is overbought and relative volume is only 0.71x; momentum chasing a thin-volume move into earnings carries gap risk.

watchlist.name: Novo Nordisk A/S
watchlist.thesis: NVO sits in a full bearish MA stack: 10.3% below 20-day MA, 13.7% below 100-day MA. 30-day EPS revisions: -3.1% cut. Earnings growth for the current year is negative at -2.2%. RSI at 38.1 is weak but not yet at a bounce-worthy extreme. Lagging its sector by 14 percentage points over 20 days.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA ~$39.43, 20-day high $43.64, ATR-based stop on any short ~$39.57 (1 ATR of $0.97 above current)
watchlist.risk: Trailing P/E of 9.5x is cheap in absolute terms; any positive clinical or regulatory headline could trigger a sharp short-cover rally.

watchlist.name: Comcast Corporation
watchlist.thesis: CMCSA at $20.66 has RSI of 26.2, the weakest on the screen. Down 16.7% from its 20-day high, 20-day momentum at -16.7%, EPS estimates cut. Earnings on 2026-10-22 are a binary risk event for the short side. Revenue revisions also negative at -0.33%.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA ~$21.95, 20-day high $25.07, ATR-based stop on any short ~$21.25 (1 ATR of $0.60 above current)
watchlist.risk: RSI this low can attract mean-reversion buyers; earnings on 10-22 are a hard stop for any short thesis, either a catalyst or a squeeze.

commodities.name: Brent crude
commodities.note: Brent at $106.76 gained 6.4% this week, now 3.2% above its 20-day MA in a bullish MA stack. 40-day momentum is +20.6%. The move is supporting XLE's bounce but note that WTI (CL=F, $93.6) is 12.3% off its 20-day high, suggesting Brent's rally may not be fully confirmed across the curve.

commodities.name: Gold
commodities.note: Gold at $4,196 is 1.5% below its 20-day MA with 20-day momentum at -3.6% and RSI 41.8. The MA stack is mixed. Safe-haven demand is not driving price right now despite geopolitical noise; watch for a reclaim of the 20-day MA as a signal of renewed bid.

commodities.name: Copper
commodities.note: Copper at $6.77 broke out on volume (rel_volume 7.6x), 2.6% above its 20-day MA and within 0.9% of its 20-day high. 20-day momentum +6.9%, bullish MA stack. This is the strongest signal of cyclical demand among commodities this week.

commodities.name: Natural gas
commodities.note: Nat gas at $3.15 is 3.3% above its 20-day MA with 20-day momentum +8.6%. MA stack is mixed and liquidity is thin; the move is directionally positive but not confirmed by volume.

commodities.name: Wheat
commodities.note: Wheat at 670.5 fell 3.1% this week, sitting 4.2% below its 20-day MA with RSI at 39.8. Momentum is negative on both 20 and 40-day frames. No catalyst visible; watch for whether corn (also weak, down 3.2% on the week) stabilises before re-engaging the grains complex.

risks: ASML earnings on 2026-10-14: a miss on EUV orders or lowered guidance would hit XLK broadly and pressure MSFT sympathy. ASML is already 5% off its 20-day high going in.
Breadth deterioration: only 3 of 11 sectors are above their 50-day MAs. A rotation out of XLK (the sole sector with strong 20-day momentum at +6%) would leave the index with little support.
CMCSA earnings on 2026-10-22 and MSFT on 2026-10-28: two large-cap prints within 10 days; elevated event-risk density for mid-to-late October.

Crude oil surge (Brent +6.4% weekly) is not yet feeding through to broader energy equities convincingly. If oil stays elevated, it raises cost-of-goods inflation risk and complicates the Fed's path, which is a headwind for high-multiple tech.
Copper breakout on thin liquidity (though vol was 7.6x): if the volume spike was a positioning event rather than genuine demand, a reversal would undercut the cyclical recovery narrative.
